title: Male Factor Infertility and Azoospermia: Obstructive vs Non-Obstructive Algorithms
subject: ss-reproductive-medicine
refs: ASRM Practice Committee Opinion on Azoospermia

steps.say: Azoospermia requires rigorous laboratory verification before assigning a definitive diagnosis. Examining two consecutive semen specimens centrifuged at 3000g for 15 minutes must show zero spermatozoa in the pellet.
steps.tx: Establishing a formal **azoospermia definition** requires strict laboratory **verification** on at least 2 separate ejaculates. Thorough microscopic inspection of the **centrifuged pellet** following centrifugation at 3000g for 15 minutes must reveal zero spermatozoa before diagnosing complete absence of ejaculated gametes. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

nodes.label: Initial semen analysis shows zero sperm

steps.say: Non-obstructive azoospermia stems from intrinsic testicular failure. Patients present with small testicular volume under 15 mL, elevated serum FSH, and underlying germ cell arrest.
steps.tx: Intrinsic testicular failure defines **non-obstructive azoospermia**, manifesting with bilaterally reduced **testicular volume** under 15 mL. Loss of negative feedback from depleted germinal epithelium drives markedly **elevated FSH**, reflecting primary spermatogenic arrest, hypospermatogenesis, or Sertoli-cell-only syndrome. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

steps.say: Obstructive azoospermia features normal hormone production alongside a physical block. The testes retain normal size, serum FSH remains normal, and physical examination reveals epididymal distension.
steps.tx: Preserved spermatogenesis characterizes **obstructive azoospermia**, where bilateral testicular volume exceeds 18 mL alongside completely **normal FSH**. Physical examination detects tense, indurated **epididymal distension** caused by fluid backpressure from a mechanical obstruction spanning from the rete testis to ejaculatory ducts. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

steps.say: Microdissection testicular sperm extraction represents the surgical gold standard for non-obstructive cases. High operating microscope magnification yields sperm retrieval rates between 40 and 60 percent.
steps.tx: Executing optical **micro-TESE** under 15x to 25x magnification is the definitive technique for non-obstructive azoospermia, achieving a **sperm retrieval rate** of 40 to 60 percent. The microsurgeon selectively identifies and biopsies opaque, dilated **seminiferous tubules** that harbor active focal spermatogenesis. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

nodes.label: Selective harvest of dilated seminiferous tubules

steps.say: Klinefelter syndrome is the most prevalent genetic cause of non-obstructive azoospermia. Patients with a 47,XXY karyotype exhibit firm micro-testes under 4 mL and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.
steps.tx: The commonest genetic cause of testicular failure is **Klinefelter syndrome**, characterized by a **47,XXY** karyotype. Men present with small firm testes under 4 mL, tall eunuchoid proportions, azoospermia, and profound **hypergonadotropic hypogonadism** resulting from progressive testicular hyalinization and tubular sclerosis. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

steps.say: Complete deletions of AZFa or AZFb indicate complete absence of sperm. Because germ cells are entirely missing, these deletions represent absolute contraindications to micro-TESE.
steps.tx: Genetic screening of the azoospermia factor region detects microdeletions of **AZFa** and **AZFb**. Complete deletions in these loci cause total germ cell aplasia or complete meiotic maturation arrest, establishing an absolute **micro-TESE contraindication** because sperm recovery probability is zero. Accurate clinical assessment and rigorous monitoring guide optimal therapeutic decisions in reproductive medicine.

left.title: Complete AZFa or AZFb Deletions
points: Loss of USP9Y, DDX3Y, or RBMY

steps.say: Isolated AZFc deletions retain favorable surgical prognosis. Microdissection yields sperm in 50 to 70 percent of men, though male offspring inherit the deletion unconditionally.
steps.tx: Men with an **AZFc deletion** involving **DAZ gene** clusters maintain islands of preserved spermatogenesis, permitting successful micro-TESE retrieval in 50 to 70 percent of cases. Couples must receive formal genetic counseling regarding obligatory **male offspring transmission**, as all sons inherit the identical deletion.

Micro-TESE retrieves sperm in 50 to 70 percent
ICSI transmits deletion to 100% of male offspring

steps.say: Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens is tied to cystic fibrosis mutations in up to 80 percent of men. Genetic carrier screening of both partners is mandatory before proceeding.
steps.tx: Physical absence of the vas deferens in **CBAVD** strongly reflects underlying **CFTR mutations**, identified in 70 to 80 percent of patients. Comprehensive **carrier screening** of the female partner is mandatory prior to ART to calculate transmission risk and guide preimplantation genetic testing.
